spec.title: Index and knowledge graph
spec.purpose: Route an agent to the right spec and the right graph node in one read. This file defines no system behaviour; it defines where behaviour is defined.

section.title: Spec map
section.text: One spec per concern, each under 1000 lines. A spec that needs more is two specs. Status: locked means the owner decided; proposed means written and awaiting the owner's card; draft means being written.

node.title: graph/: one JSON node per file, graph.sh add/edge/find/check/index/sync-specs
node.text: The graph is the source; specs cite it. See s-graph.

section.text: SPEC-00 index and knowledge graph (this file). SPEC-01 conventions: naming, UTC, contents lists, GOOD and NEVER, config and variables, status codes, event log. SPEC-02 roles and permissions. SPEC-03 DAG workflow and node contract. SPEC-04 herdr seat lifecycle. SPEC-05 compaction and checkpoint. SPEC-06 control plane. SPEC-07 SITREP site and factory dashboard. SPEC-08 player contract and runtimes. SPEC-09 game adapters (Qud, Cities Skylines 2). SPEC-10 game hosts. SPEC-11 pane renderer and plugin manifest, SPEC-11.B Rust terminal. SPEC-12 delivery. SPEC-13 testing and lint. SPEC-14 skills. SPEC-15 SDLC DAG end to end. SPEC-16 (specs/scheduler) the Go scheduler, one file per domain. SPEC-17 orchestrator and agent health: one board is the intake, the orchestrator runs the line, the system checks every agent, halt and bring-up, the status code map.

section.title: The knowledge graph
section.text: graph/nodes/<id>.json, one file per node, written only by graph/bin/graph.sh. N agents add nodes at once: distinct files, no lock, no merge conflict. The Architect runs graph.sh find before cutting any ticket; a ticket that contradicts a locked Decision node is refused by the reviewer.

Node id = PREFIX-slug. Prefixes: DEC Decision, REQ Requirement, CMP Component, IFC Interface, SCH Schema, WFL Workflow, NOD DAG node, ROL Role, SPK Spike, RSK Risk, STC StatusCode, RUN Runbook. Status: draft, proposed, locked, superseded. A locked node is never edited; a change is a new node with a supersedes edge.

Edge kinds: depends_on, implements, decided_by, verified_by, risks, owned_by, defined_in, supersedes. Every edge target must exist (graph.sh check, exit 3 names the offender). graph.sh index renders graph/INDEX.md and graph/GRAPH.mmd; both are generated and never edited.
Sources on a node name where it came from: owner:<card or message id>:<UTC>, research:<url>, spec:<SPEC-NN>. A Decision node without an owner source is a defect.
section.mermaid: flowchart LR OWNER[Owner card or message] -- source --> DEC[DEC node, locked] DEC -- decided_by --> CMP[CMP, IFC, ROL nodes] CMP -- verified_by --> SPK[SPK spike] CMP -- risks --> RSK[RSK risk] SPEC[SPEC-NN.xml] -- ref node --> CMP ARCH[Architect] -- graph.sh find --> DEC ARCH -- cuts --> WO[work-order ticket]

section.title: Pointers between specs
section.text: A spec never restates another spec. It points: ref spec="SPEC-NN" anchor="section-id" for a section, ref node="PREFIX-slug" for a graph node. make lint resolves every pointer; a dangling one fails the build. A spec section that would exceed its budget becomes a new SPEC-NN.X file with a pointer left behind.

section.title: Rules every spec obeys
section.text: Valid against specs/schema/spec.xsd (make lint, xmllint in Podman). contents first, every section listed in order. Under 1000 lines. UTC in updated. One owner source per locked Decision. Every node declared in a spec exists in graph/ with the same title (graph.sh sync-specs). No em dash anywhere. No prose addressed to another agent: a spec speaks to whoever reads it, in definitions.
